prompt.en: According to the passage, the surah opens with a code of conduct: first the manners owed to Allah and His Messenger, then the manners believers owe one another.

explanation.en: The essay opens by saying the surah lays down a code of conduct, the manners a believer owes to Allah and His Messenger first, then the manners believers owe one another.

anchor.quote: first the manners a believer owes to Allah and His Messenger, then the manners believers owe one another

prompt.en: "By my life, you struck pickaxes by the ear of the Messenger of God for your father and his faruq." Who said this?

explanation.en: Imam al-Husayn addressed these words to Aisha, citing the verse against raising voices above the Prophet's and recalling what was done by the ear of the Messenger of God.

anchor.quote: By my life, you struck pickaxes by the ear of the Messenger of God for your father and his faruq

prompt.en: In the narration to Zurara on verse 6, what does Imam al-Baqir say about every verse of the Quran?

options.en: It has an outer sense and an inner sense.
It has only its plain, literal meaning.
It must be verified before it is believed.
It was revealed about one particular person.

explanation.en: Teaching Zurara, Imam al-Baqir says no verse of the Quran lacks an outer and an inner sense; what people hold is its outer, and what he disclosed is its inner.

anchor.quote: no verse of the Quran lacks an outer and an inner sense

prompt.en: The believer is the brother of the believer, his eye and his ____.

explanation.en: In this saying the believer is the believer's brother, his eye and his guide, one who does not betray, wrong, disparage, or break a promise to him.

anchor.quote: The believer is the brother of the believer, his eye and his guide

prompt.en: In the passage's perspectives, one reading notes the Quran still calls the fighters "believers." What does it take this to prove?

options.en: That fighting between believers is always forbidden.
That the two sides had already made peace.
That grave disobedience does not expel a person from faith.
That both groups lost their faith by fighting.

explanation.en: The perspectives note that the Quran still calls the fighters 'believers,' which one reading takes as proof that grave disobedience does not expel a person from faith.

anchor.quote: the Quran still calls the fighters 'believers,' which he and al-Bukhari take as proof that grave disobedience does not expel a person from faith

prompt.en: According to the essay, defaming a fellow believer harms only the one defamed and not the person who does it.

explanation.en: The essay says Tabrisi reads the believers as a single self, so that to wrong a brother is to wrong oneself; the harm falls on the one defaming too.

anchor.quote: Tabrisi takes the believers as a single self, so that to wrong a brother is to wrong oneself

prompt.en: In the passage, what does Imam al-Sadiq say happens when a believer accuses his brother?

options.en: His faith dissolves like salt in water.
His prayers are rejected for forty days.
He must free a slave to atone.
The brother's wrongdoing passes onto him.

explanation.en: Imam al-Sadiq says that when a believer accuses his brother, faith melts from the heart the way salt dissolves in water, so grave is the act.

anchor.quote: When a believer accuses his brother, faith dissolves in his heart as salt dissolves in water.

prompt.en: "Do not swear, O man. Better than me is whoever is more Godwary toward Allah and more obedient to Him. By Allah, this verse has not been abrogated." Who said this?

explanation.en: Imam al-Rida told a man not to swear, affirming that whoever is more Godwary and obedient to Allah is the better one, and that the verse was never abrogated.

anchor.quote: Do not swear, O man. Better than me is whoever is more Godwary toward Allah and more obedient to Him. By Allah, this verse has not been abrogated.

prompt.en: According to the perspectives, how do the Shia narrations press the islam and iman distinction further?

options.en: Islam and iman mean exactly the same thing.
Faith enters the heart before any outward submission.
True iman also requires recognising the Imams' authority.
The Bedouins were hypocrites with no share in Islam.

explanation.en: The perspectives say the Shia narrations push the distinction further: a man may be a Muslim without being a believer, and true faith also means recognising the Imams' authority.

anchor.quote: a man may be a Muslim without being a believer, and true iman also requires recognising 'this matter,' the Imams' authority

prompt.en: The surah ends with God, who knows the Unseen and watches every deed - ____, Tabatabai says, for all that it has commanded.

explanation.en: Tabatabai reads the closing verse, that God knows the Unseen and watches every deed, as a seal set over everything the surah has commanded.

anchor.quote: The surah ends with God, who knows the Unseen and watches every deed - a seal, Tabatabai says, for all that it has commanded.
